title: FuzzSplore: Visualizing Feedback-Driven Fuzzing Techniques
review_status: full-text audit complete; four linked visual views, intended analyst workflow, AFL++ scope, stochastic t-SNE caveat, target-specific proxy motivation, and absence of controlled analyst/outcome evaluation checked
sections_checked: Abstract and introduction: proxy-metric and target-overfitting motivation
Sections 3.1–3.3: data retrieval, four visualization views, analyst feedback loop
venue_year_verified: arXiv preprint v2, submitted 2021-02-06; no peer-reviewed venue verified
evidence_note: Proposes an AFL++-based dashboard with testcase scatterplot/t-SNE, coverage growth, interesting-testcase, and generation-graph views to help analysts compare configurations on a single target. Paper demonstrates implementation but reports no recruited analyst study, task-completion measure, or downstream bug-yield test. t-SNE is stochastic and dataset-dependent. A later 2026 TOSEM task taxonomy includes FuzzSplore as covering five of its analysis-task IDs, but this is task support mapping, not usability validation.

title: A Probabilistic Framework for Mutation Testing in Deep Neural Networks
review_status: full-text audit complete; motivation, Bayesian PMT procedure, sampled training instances, selected mutations, approximation/cost analysis, empirical threshold caveats, validity threats, and authors' open debate on valid DNN mutations checked
sections_checked: Sections 2–4: experiment procedure, posterior definitions, effect and error criteria
Section 5: MNIST/MovieLens/UnityEyes experiments, eight operators, cost/approximation results
Sections 6 and 8: threats, mutation-validity debate, conclusion/future work
venue_year_verified: Information and Software Technology 155 (2023), article 107129; DOI 10.1016/j.infsof.2022.107129; arXiv v1 submitted 2022-08-11
evidence_note: PMT estimates a posterior/graded mutation effect rather than a binary kill result; evaluation uses three model/dataset families and eight operators, with 200 trained instances in the main analysis and bootstrap/error studies. Authors describe empirical similarity-ratio thresholds as a practical scale and acknowledge model/operator scope, approximation error, and debate over valid DNN mutations. It improves consistency in these tests but does not validate scores against real production DNN faults.

title: Selecting Initial Seeds for Better JVM Fuzzing
review_status: full-text audit complete; three JVMs/two fuzzers, 10 selection strategies, corpus construction, five-repeat/24-hour design, seed-budget tables, inconsistency and developer-triaged bug outcomes, and validity threats checked
sections_checked: Sections II–III: JVM fuzzers and 10 seed-selection strategies
Section IV: three JVMs, P1/P2 benchmark corpora and GitHub-derived P3 corpus, measurement definitions
Section V: Tables IV–IX, repeated-run/budget outcomes and developer bug reports
Sections VI–VIII: implications, threats to validity, conclusion
evidence_note: Across HotSpot/OpenJ9/Bisheng JDK, JavaTailor/VECT and the selected corpora, the study reports strong FISSCFG results at tested seed budgets and about 30 seconds of extraction/selection overhead. It separately reports 25 previously unknown bugs, 21 marked confirmed or fixed by developers (not all necessarily fixed), seven found only with the open-source corpus. Results remain bounded by three JVMs, two fuzzers, selected corpora, and 24-hour runs; the open-source corpus and alternative selectors provide complementary/per-row counterevidence.

title: Visualization Task Taxonomy to Understand the Fuzzing Internals
review_status: targeted follow-up; official ACM article/abstract and results summary checked for number of practitioner interviews, taxonomy size, tool coverage, and FuzzSplore mapping; full methods/data not re-audited
sections_checked: ACM abstract and reported results: 33 practitioner interviews, 120 tasks, six existing tools collectively support 10 tasks
FuzzSplore task-coverage row in the existing-tool comparison
evidence_note: Later task taxonomy reports 120 desired visualization analysis tasks from 33 practitioner interviews; six existing tools collectively support 10 tasks, and FuzzSplore is mapped to five IDs. This identifies a task-coverage gap, not proof of usability failure or tool ineffectiveness for its supported tasks.

title: muPRL: A Mutation Testing Pipeline for Deep Reinforcement Learning based on Real Faults
review_status: targeted follow-up; arXiv abstract checked for real-fault-derived mutation operators and scope; full text not audited
sections_checked: Abstract: repository-mined real RL faults, derived mutation operators, and strong-vs-weak test-generator discrimination
venue_year_verified: arXiv preprint first submitted 2024-08-27; venue not independently verified
evidence_note: Adjacent counterpoint that uses faults mined from deep-RL repositories to derive mutation operators. It studies reinforcement learning rather than the supervised DNN settings of the sampled PMT paper, so it does not validate PMT's thresholds or transfer across regimes.

title: New Formulation of DNN Statistical Mutation Killing for Ensuring Monotonicity: A Technical Report

evidence_note: Addresses monotonicity of the earlier DeepCrime statistical mutant-killing criterion. It is not described as a direct empirical validation or replacement evaluation of PMT; that distinction is preserved.
